children: Manufacturing expansion, R&D spending and supplier development form the core of the seven-year investment plan

Hyundai Motor Group plans to invest USD 15.5 billion in India between 2026 and 2032, covering manufacturing expansion, research and development (R&D), local supply chains and emerging mobility technologies. The investment was discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung in New Delhi on 13 October. The plan positions India as a key market for the group’s growth and export strategy, while supporting its efforts to expand local production and develop automotive technologies.

The investment will support capacity expansion across Hyundai Motor India and Kia India to meet domestic demand and strengthen India’s role as an export base. The group currently has annual vehicle production capacity of more than 1.4 million units across its facilities in Chennai, Pune and Anantapur.

Hyundai Motor India’s Chennai facility has a capacity of 824,000 units, while its Pune plant has a capacity of 170,000 units. Kia India’s Anantapur facility can produce 431,000 units annually. The group expects capacity at Pune to increase in phases.

Hyundai Motor Group plans to develop its Indian R&D infrastructure and expand local technical capabilities. Around USD 700 million is earmarked for its R&D centre, including a vehicle testing track, to support next-generation automotive technology development.
The group also plans to build local talent in engineering and research, with India expected to play a greater role in its technology development network.

The investment will also target supplier development and greater localisation of vehicle components. Hyundai plans to work with regional partners to strengthen supply-chain resilience and identify local suppliers.

In emerging mobility, the group will explore opportunities involving startups, mobility services, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, specialised automotive financing and end-of-life vehicle recycling. It will establish a dedicated investment entity in India to coordinate capital deployment, partnerships and projects across these areas.

Hyundai Motor Group employs more than 24,000 people in India. The proposed investment is expected to generate jobs across manufacturing, engineering, R&D and supplier networks, while building skills in advanced automotive technologies.

The group’s affiliates, including Hyundai Mobis, Hyundai Transys, Hyundai Capital, Hyundai Wia and Hyundai Glovis, already operate across components, services and related activities in India. The investment could deepen these linkages, with the overall impact depending on how projects are implemented through 2032.
